summary: Discrepant ack timing between SDKs and edge HTTP proxy causing confusing retry behavior for function/tool calls
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports unexpected duplicate downstream tool/function invocations when client aborts and retries streaming/function-calling requests. Behavior differs across SDKs: TS clients observe a single execution most of the time, Go sometimes sees duplicates, and Python sees duplicates more predictably. Customer is using a managed edge HTTP proxy (third-party) in front of Redwood API for routing.

Impact:
- Potential double side-effects in customer's downstream systems (webhooks, DB writes).
- Customer running on Dedicated plan; high business impact for some requests.

High level ask: explain root cause and provide immediate mitigations and clear SDK guidance (and docs) to avoid duplicate tool/function invocations on client-side retries and mid-stream aborts.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use Python SDK to open a streaming function-call session to redwood-3b-v2 via customer's edge proxy (proxy with connection pooling).
2) Trigger a long-running function call (customer provided test harness that invokes external webhook).
3) Mid-stream, cancel the client connection (SIGINT/close socket) and immediately retry the same logical request with the same idempotency token (client code uses per-session nonce).
4) Observe: external webhook receives 2 POSTs in ~500-1500ms window. Repeat with TS and Go SDKs and compare behavior.
logs:
Customer-provided logs (trimmed):
- python-client: 'stream closed by client' then 'reconnect using idempotency: nonce=3f6a...
POST /v1/streams 200 OK'
- edge-proxy logs: 'connection reused, header-length-truncated: idempotency-token=3f6a...->3f6'
- webhook logs: two deliveries timestamped 2026-03-01T14:22:10.123Z and 2026-03-01T14:22:11.349Z
- go-client: 'request retried, idempotency token present' but sometimes '200 processed' twice.
- ts-client: mostly single delivery; occasional duplicate in older proxy instances.
Relevant traces: link: https://redwood.internal/traces/trace-abc123 (customer-supplied)
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: header rewriting/truncation at edge-proxy + SDK connection-pool reuse causes mismatch between what the SDK thinks it sent as the idempotency token and what the service actually received. Specific observations:
- Edge proxy truncates headers above ~1KB when reusing persistent connections; the customer's per-session idempotency token included extra metadata (base64 + signed salt) pushing it over threshold. Truncation appears non-deterministic depending on connection reuse and chunking.
- Python SDK historically sets a per-stream idempotency nonce and then reuses the same http2 connection with the header in the initial request metadata. If the proxy rewrites the header during connection reuse, the server treats the retry as a new idempotency key and re-executes the function.
- TS SDK performs per-request header injection (on each retry it regenerates the header), reducing chance of mismatch; Go SDK behavior depends on http client usage and whether user code constructed a single client vs per-request.
- We reproduced a truncated header in lab by configuring our internal envoy to simulate customer's proxy behavior. When truncated, server writes indicate a different idempotency key (shortened).
- No evidence of server-side double-execute due to internal retries: server logs show two distinct keys arriving.

Next steps suggested:
- Recommend immediate customer mitigation + patch in SDKs to canonicalize idempotency header generation and fallback detection.
- Patch request queued for SDKs to ensure per-retry header regeneration or authoritative header re-transmit on reconnect.
- Edge guidance: recommend proxy config to not truncate headers and to preserve header casing and content length.
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Patel: Customer opened with webhook timestamps and proxy vendor details (FastFrontier Edge v2.1). Customer attached minimal repro harness for Python and Go.

2026-03-01 Samir Gupta: Assigned to SRE/SDK triage. Initial guess: header truncation at proxy + idempotency token size/encoding. Requested full proxy logs and example raw HTTP header dumps from customer.

2026-03-02 Customer (Streamline AI): Provided proxy debug logs and confirmed they run connection pooling with header size limit 1024 bytes. They also confirmed they observed duplicates only when using their custom auth metadata added into idempotency tokens (we asked for sample).

2026-03-02 Jordan Lee (SDK lead): Reproduced with envoy config; confirmed truncation reproduces duplicate executions for Python. Opened experimental branch to change Python SDK to regenerate idempotency header on retry. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/985

2026-03-03 Samir Gupta: Suggested immediate customer workaround: (1) reduce idempotency token payload size by switching to compact UUID (v4) instead of signed blob; (2) temporarily disable proxy header truncation or increase limit; (3) set SDK retry policy to 'no-auto-retry' for these function-calling endpoints until patch applied.
2026-03-03 Streamline AI: Will test reducing token size and report by EOD. Asked for short-term config snippet for disabling automatic retry in Python SDK.
2026-03-03 Priya Patel: Shared example: python client with client_opts.retries=0 and regenerate idempotency token per-request. Also linked to KB draft for docs update.
resolution:
WORKAROUND PROVIDED — In Progress to patch SDKs and docs.
Short-term workarounds provided to customer:
- Use compact, short idempotency keys (UUID v4) instead of large signed blobs.
- Configure edge proxy to increase header size limit and avoid truncation on connection reuse.
- Set SDK retry policy to disable automatic client-side retries for function-calling/streaming endpoints until SDK patch deployed.

Planned long-term fixes:
- SDKs (Python/Go/TS): implement per-retry idempotency header regeneration and add detection for truncated/changed idempotency token returned by server -> surface clear error to client instead of silently re-executing.
- Docs: add dedicated guidance for idempotency token size, proxy interoperability, and recommended header placement.
- Confluence runbook: add steps for SRE to debug edge-proxy header truncation.

Related PRs and patches:
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/985 (experimental, will add tests)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/462 (WIP)
- Docs draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPPORT/Idempotency+and+Edge+Proxies (draft)
